videos.title: WWDC26: Principles of great design | Apple
videos.why: Apple's designers name eight principles behind their apps (purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity, flexibility, simplicity, craft, delight); as you watch, count how few of them are about how things look.

videos.title: Minimalism is Getting Absurd: Updating Dieter Rams' 10 Principles
videos.why: An industrial designer revisits Rams' ten principles and argues where minimalism has drifted into a style for its own sake; keep the Vitsœ page open to compare his updates with the originals.

podcasts.episode: 1. What is UX, anyway? (feat. Dr. Jakob Nielsen, the usability guru)
podcasts.why: Jakob Nielsen explains what user experience covers and how the field has changed since NN/g started in 1998; listen for how far beyond the screen he draws the boundary.

podcasts.episode: Barry Katz: The history and philosophy of design in Silicon Valley and beyond
podcasts.why: A design historian on when design became part of how technology companies work, and where the familiar friction between designers and engineers comes from.

reads.title: The Definition of User Experience (UX)
reads.why: Don Norman and Jakob Nielsen's short definition; read it for the distinction it draws between the whole experience and the user interface, which is the core idea of this lesson.

reads.title: The power of good design
reads.why: Dieter Rams' ten principles for good design, one short paragraph each, ending with 'less, but better'; test your current product against each one.

reads.title: Meet the Elements
reads.source: Jesse James Garrett, The Elements of User Experience (free sample chapter, PDF)
reads.why: The chapter that introduces the five planes, from strategy at the bottom to surface at the top; the diagrams are the source of the UX planes figure in this lesson.
